name: Agentic CRM for Pharma
blurb: AI agents in the systems field teams use with doctors.
title: Agentic CRM for Pharma
answer: Pharma CRM is being rebuilt around AI agents that prepare calls, suggest next actions and draft follow ups. Salesforce's Agentforce Life Sciences was chosen by Takeda, then by Novartis and AstraZeneca in December 2025 and Chiesi in April 2026, and Salesforce reports more than 140 life sciences organisations using it.

reading.body:
Salesforce has consolidated pharma field engagement onto one agent platform, with Takeda, Novartis, AstraZeneca and Chiesi all selecting Agentforce Life Sciences and more than 140 life sciences organisations reported using it.

The pattern is a single vendor accumulating the largest commercial teams in the industry in under two years. Takeda came first, Novartis and AstraZeneca followed in December 2025, and Chiesi in April 2026. Each of these is a global customer engagement platform decision, which means the agents that prepare calls, suggest next actions and draft follow ups sit in the same system the field force already uses.

For AI specifically, the constraint is not model quality but what the output is allowed to be. Any agent output that reaches a doctor is promotional material under review, so the platform choice matters less than the content rules wrapped around it. That is why adoption here looks like procurement of a governed system rather than experimentation with a tool.

The data does not say how many of the 140 organisations are live versus contracted, what the agents cost, or whether they improved any commercial outcome. It also does not cover the competing platforms these companies may still run alongside Agentforce.

terms.line: The field of computer science dedicated to creating systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence: understanding language, recognizing patterns, making decisions.
The 2026 package of targeted amendments to the EU AI Act, deferring high-risk deadlines and restructuring conformity assessment.

An AI system that takes a goal, breaks it into steps, and carries those steps out using tools, rather than answering a single question and stopping. The defining trait is initiative between instructions: the agent decides what to do next.

explainer:
Customer relationship management systems in pharma record every interaction field teams have with health care professionals, plan visits and manage approved content. The newest generation embeds AI agents that prepare a representative before a visit, summarising the doctor's specialty, past interactions and relevant approved materials, suggest the next best action, and draft follow up messages for approval.

The rapid adoption by large drugmakers since 2025 reflects the promise of more relevant engagement with less administrative work. The constraints come from promotional regulation: anything an agent drafts that reaches a health care professional is promotional material, must stay within the approved label and must pass review, and interactions must be logged. Configuring agents to draw only on approved content, and keeping a person responsible for what is sent, is what makes them usable.
